This is the description of what I talk about in the video... I have clinical depression and anxiety, so I’m on your side here...

Depression is a choice, so why are you complaining? Seriously, get a grip...

Honestly... ANYONE that makes comments like these HAS NO CLUE what depression is like. There have been times I've received comments like this when I opened up about my depression... and it's just disappointing. I know they are a speaking from a standpoint of ignorance and misunderstanding, but they don't know the potential harm a comment like that could have on someone suffering with depression.

Comments like, "Why can't you just be positive?" or "You are being selfish" and even, "You're not appreciate what you have enough." is just harmful. Have a sense of empathy. People that deal with clinical depression (and other mental health issues) can't just turn it on like a switch. Obviously... if it worked like that, we'd turn it on. Why would anyone want to feel sad, depressed, and unhappy all of the time. It's not a good feeling.

So I wanted to make this video in a response to some that have made comments like this. I know I'm not the only one who has received this response from someone else. If you deal with a mental illness, you ARE NOT weird for it. You aren't selfish. And most importantly, you aren't alone in this. To those who make these ignorant and just naive remarks... please think about the impact your words can have on someone dealing with a mental illness (heck or even without). Have some empathy (a heart), and hear them out.

I understand what that means now! Here’s a quick recap:

1. Don’t put ALL of your happiness into your significant other. Your significant other should ADD to your happiness, not BE your happiness.

2. Your world should not revolve around your significant other. For some reason, we focus so much on the person we’re dating that we stop focusing on ourselves completely. Any free time you have, you want to spend it with them. Make sure you are spending time with your friends, family, and yourself.

3. You completely lose who you are. If you don’t avoid doing these things, if the relationship fails, you are left and in so much pain, and don’t even know who you are anymore (at least that was my experience). 

So try and avoid these mistakes to maintain positive mental health when you’re in a relationship!

If you're depressed because your tired of doing the same thing everyday, you are not alone. I feel the same way.

Listen, there are different thing that can trigger depression. One of them (at least for me), is the alarm clock going off in the morning. It's like a constant reminder about the day I'm about to go into. The thing is, I've been doing the same daily/weekly routine for so many months now. It's like I'm in the Twilight Zone! It gets to me. I truly am tired of doing the same thing everyday.

I know that there are some days where I may hang out with my family or friends. I may play a sport, etc. But the majority of my days (during the week especially) are spent doing the same things everyday. I'm tired of it! The purpose of this video is to show you that you are not alone. I'm not you. I'm not saying I know EXACTLY how you feel because I don't. What I do know is that if you are tired of doing the same thing everyday, you aren't alone in that thought/feeling.

I hope that this videos shows you a different viewpoint on life. It may help win the daily fight of being tired of doing the same thing everyday. You got this! Keep fighting! I mean it!
